newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian workers protest over painful reforms.
newsitem.headline: Romanian workers protest over painful reforms.

text.p: Thousands of industrial workers marched across the Romanian capital on Thursday in the biggest anti-government protest since the centrists' election win over ex-communists last year.
Up to 10,000 protesters, shouting "We voted for you and you betrayed us" filed past the government building in central Bucharest, which was ringed by anti-riot troops and gendarmes.
Many factory workers said they had come by train or by bus from remote areas of Romania for the rally staged by union leaders in central Revolution Square in brilliant sunshine.

Thursday's protest marked the end of the honeymoon for Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, as big labour unions flex their muscles to wrest concessions from the government on its plans to restructure big communist-era industries.
"We gave them a period of grace to deliver on their promises," said Vasile Cristea, leader of unions representing workers from carmakers to weapons industry suppliers.
Cristea said labour unions had urged the government to draft a strategy for the future of industry, with retraining for workers made redundant under restructuring.
The protesters also demanded cuts in income taxes, saying their earnings had been dented by rises in fuel and electricity prices as part of price of liberalisation earlier this year.
"Poverty has no political colour nor has the need for job security to raise our children decently," Cristea said.
Average Romanian monthly pay is around $60. Official data show that Romanians' purchasing power has been halved since the 1989 collapse of communism.
The centrists have vowed to speed up reforms, including privatisation of large sectors of the economy, in exchange for resumed credits from international lenders.
Discontent with the transition to a free-market system weighed heavily in the centrist victory last November, ending the ex-communists' seven-year grip on power.
Ciorbea will address Romanians next week on progress in fulfilling promises in the government's first 200 days in office.
